paths.summary: Add an SSD and a second RAM module to keep this laptop fast for office work.
next_steps: Buy a 500 GB M.2 2280 NVMe SSD and an 8 GB DDR4 SO-DIMM.
Back up your data, then install the SSD and clone the old drive.
Insert the RAM module into the free slot.
paths.why: Replacing the hard drive with an SSD is the biggest speed gain for office work, and the laptop has a free M.2 slot and RAM slot.
assumptions: Sample part prices; no labour cost.
safety: Unplug the charger and disconnect the battery before opening the case.

claims.text: The laptop has an M.2 2280 slot that supports NVMe SSDs.
One of two DDR4 slots is free, supporting up to 32 GB.

paths.summary: Replace the worn battery; the rest of the laptop is in good shape.
next_steps: Remove the two battery screws and swap the pack.
paths.why: The battery has lost about a quarter of its capacity, and it can be swapped without special tools.
assumptions: Battery health readings may be inaccurate on some firmware.
safety: Do not use a swollen battery; take it to a repair shop.

claims.text: The battery is customer-replaceable and secured by two screws.

paths.summary: Give it to someone who needs a laptop for office or school work.
next_steps: Reset the operating system and securely erase the drive.
Offer it to a school, a student, or a local reuse initiative.
paths.why: The laptop still runs a supported operating system, but the environmental benefit depends on the recipient not buying a new one.
assumptions: The recipient would otherwise buy a new laptop.
unverified: Whether a local recipient needs this device.

claims.text: The CPU is on the supported processor list.
Drives should be securely erased before passing on.

paths.summary: Only salvage parts if nobody can use the laptop as a whole.
next_steps: Keep the laptop in use or pass it on first.
paths.why: The device still works, so taking it apart wastes more value than it recovers.
unverified: A reuse channel for individual parts.

paths.summary: Recycle it at a certified e-waste point once no other option fits.
next_steps: Bring it to a certified e-waste collection point.
paths.why: Recycling recovers materials but gives the device no further use.
safety: Remove nothing yourself; recyclers handle batteries safely.

claims.text: Securely erase drives before handing over a computer.

passages.title: Example Laptop 14 Hardware Maintenance Manual
passages.text: The computer has two SO-DIMM DDR4 slots and supports up to 32 GB of memory. No memory is soldered to the system board.

passages.title: Example Laptop 14 Hardware Maintenance Manual
passages.text: The battery is a customer-replaceable unit secured by two screws. Replacement packs are available under part number EX-BAT-57.

passages.text: Example CPU i5-8250U is listed as a supported processor.

passages.title: Guide to reusing and donating computers
passages.text: Before passing on a computer, reset the operating system and securely erase all drives.
